subject: FinLedger — model bridge recommendations & parity acceptance plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finledger.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: FinLedger evaluation priorities & proposed model bridge

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear evaluation path.

Call highlights
- Primary flows: KYC summarization (extraction + short rationale), customer support triage (intent + routing), and regulatory snippet extraction.
- Data: you confirmed ~12k annotated QA pairs and a larger unlabelled corpus (~1.2M tokens) we can use for cost/latency sims.
- Constraints: 95th%-ile inference latency target ≤ 300ms for the support microservice, target amortized per-request cost ≤ $0.15.
- Risk priorities: factuality/hallucination is higher priority than micro-improvements in BLEU; false positives on PII redaction are critical.

Proposed candidate models (initial sweep)
1) Llama-3-70B (int8 + KV cache) — strong instruction-following baseline for extraction tasks; cheaper ops when quantized.
2) Mistral-Instruct-30B — promising on short-form summarization, lower token-cost.
3) Redwood-Redstone-16B (our compact throughput variant) — lower latency, tuned for KV-cache heavy workloads.
4) Videx-v2 (your proprietary baseline) — provided by you in the call as the internal reference for parity.

Suggested evaluation plan (short summary)
- Dataset: run 1,000 holdout examples you provided (we'll use the attached finledger_p0_testset.csv) + 100 adversarial prompts for hallucination checks.
- Metrics: top-line extraction accuracy, hallucination rate (human spot-check), 95th%-ile token latency, and per-request token cost.
- Parity definition (proposal): open candidate considered "parity" if it meets BOTH:
  • extraction accuracy within 2 percentage points of Videx-v2 on P0 set, AND
  • human-measured hallucination rate ≤ 1.2x Videx-v2.
- Acceptance gates: if a model fails accuracy but beats latency/cost by >30%, we recommend a focused reweighting prompt strategy and a second pass with a lightweight reranker.

Artifacts attached / links
- finledger_sample_prompts.jsonl (attached) — sample prompt bundle and canonical expected outputs.
- finledger_p0_testset.csv (attached) — the 1,000-item P0 test set we discussed.
- Benchmark notebook + evaluation harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fInLedgerEvalExample
- HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/FL-2027-092

Immediate asks
1) Please confirm acceptance criteria above (accuracy/hallucination thresholds) or share alternative thresholds you need.
2) Grant a temporary S3 read role for the p0 bucket (we'll only pull the test set and anonymized samples).
3) Let us know if legal needs to review a short evaluation addendum (we can surface a minimal DPA extension).

Next steps (proposed)
- If confirmed, we kick off a 2-week parity sprint: week 1 — automated runs + latency/cost sims; week 2 — human spot-checks and final readout.
- Deliverable: a short Scorecard (accuracy, hallucination, latency, cost) + recommended production model and a runbook for rollback/fallback.

Thanks — I captured these in the Drive folder. I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff once you confirm.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

2) Hallucination measurement: your human spot-check approach sounds good. Can you define sampling methodology (random + edge-case stratification) so we can audit?
3) Data access: we'll provision a temporary S3 role but need confirmation you won't persist raw samples outside the evaluation bucket.

- Can you include a quick regression checklist for post-deploy monitoring (we want to avoid silent regressions after a quant change)?

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: FinLedger evaluation priorities & proposed model bridge

Looping you both in to propose the concrete evaluation plan and parity gates given Elena's questions.

Proposed evaluation definition (detailed)
- Accuracy: absolute-point parity = within 2.0 percentage points of Videx-v2 on the P0 extraction metric (so 86.5% would be acceptable if Videx=88.5%).
- Hallucination: human spot-check sample of 100 items stratified across: random (50), high-uncertainty (25) flagged by confidence scores, and edge-cases from regulatory categories (25). Hallucination rate must be ≤ 1.2x Videx-v2 (so if Videx=4% target ≤ 4.8%).
- Latency: 95th%-ile token-latency ≤ 300ms on our Dedicated-like configuration; cold-starts excluded.
- Cost: amortized per-request token cost ≤ $0.15 to be competitive for your production SLA.

Test matrix and runs
- Automated runs: run the 4 candidates (Llama-3-70B, Mistral-Instruct-30B, Redstone-16B, Videx-v2) across the P0 set and 3 beam/prompt variants (baseline, high-precision instructions, reranker-pass).
- Human evaluation: spot-check 100 examples per top-2 candidates. Use the attached prompt bundle for canonical scoring.
- Regression harness: run nightly drift checks against a 5k-anchor set; trigger alert if accuracy drops >1.5 points or hallucination increases >20% vs baseline.

Acceptance / playbook recommendations
- If an open model hits parity on accuracy but exceeds hallucination target, run a lightweight reranker or constrained decoding (we have a plug-in reranker that reduces hallucination in ~30% of failing cases).
- If latency is too high: evaluate Redstone-16B with quantization and KV cache tuning; this is often the quickest path to meet latency gate with minor accuracy loss.

Timeline (if Elena approves today)
- Day 0-2: credentialing + data pull + infra carve-out.
- Day 3-7: automated runs + baseline scorecard.
- Day 8-12: human spot-checks + knob tuning.
- Day 13-14: final readout + recommended model and rollback runbook.

I will prepare the quick regression checklist and a short runbook for the evaluation addendum. Aisha — I can draft the S3 access statement and the 30-day retention note for legal review.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
